What comes up in Baulkham Hills

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. What follows is how this work normally runs in the area, not a reading of any one block.

Knockdown then a benched cut

The standard Baulkham Hills sequence, and the two halves are better planned as one job.

How it is handled
Structure removed, then the cut taken in benches from the high side to the nominated platform level.
What does it
Midi to large excavator able to work on a grade, truck and dog for the volume.

Slab and footings out for a new design

Whether they come out depends entirely on what is going on top, and it is cheaper settled before the quote.

How it is handled
Broken out with a hammer where the new design needs the ground back, or left and built over where it does not.
What does it
Excavator with a hydraulic hammer and a grading bucket to finish the level.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Baulkham Hills

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Sloping established blocks Which bring site cut, benching and retaining into work that would be flat elsewhere.
  • Older housing on generous lots Room to work, and usually room to sort material rather than cart it mixed.
  • Shale derived clay soils Reactive, heavy when wet and slow to dry out after rain.
  • Dual occupancy and knockdown rebuild The dominant job types, with services and boundaries to settle before anything comes down.

Baulkham Hills streets take a tipper comfortably and many will take a truck and dog, which matters because a cut on a sloping block produces real volume. The fall decides where the machine works from and how the benches are taken.

Baulkham Hills questions

What people ask before we start

How much material comes off a sloping block?
More than people expect, and it is set by the fall and the platform level rather than by the footprint. Send the engineer levels and the volume can be worked out properly instead of estimated.
What happens to clay spoil after rain?
It gets heavier and harder to handle. Where the programme allows, the cut waits for the ground rather than fighting it, because wet clay costs more to cart and is harder to place.
Most of these blocks slope. Does that change the scope?
Usually yes. A fall across the block brings site cut, benching and sometimes retaining into a scope that would be flat work elsewhere, and it sets where a machine can safely stand while it works.
Who actually removes the asbestos?
Licensed asbestos removalists do the removal. Max holds demolition licence AD214737 and builds the programme around them, and an independent licensed assessor handles the air monitoring and the clearance. You are dealing with one contract rather than three.
